newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P assigns public info ratings to nine HK banks.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns public info ratings to nine HK banks.

text.p: Standard and Poor's said on Tuesday it had assigned public information ratings to nine Hong Kong financial institutions.
The rating agency assigned A-pi ratings to Bank of America (Asia) Ltd and Hang Seng Bank Ltd.
It gave BBB-pi ratings to Bank of East Asia Ltd, Chekiang First Bank Ltd, Dah Sing Bank Ltd, Nanyang Commercial Bank Ltd, Po Sang Bank Ltd, Shanghai Commercial Bank Ltd and Wing Lung Bank Ltd.
The "pi" ratings are based on publicly disclosed information and do not rely on S&P receiving ongoing access to management, it said in a statement.
S&P said the nine banks would have to deal with intensified competition, traditionally volatile prices and liquidity pressures as a result of possible event risk.

But the sound financial profile of many local banks, the stable economy and the established role of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority would enable the system to manage the risk, the rating agency said.
S&P said Hong Kong's banking sector was highly concentrated in two banks -- Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp, a unit of HSBC Holdings Plc, and the Bank of China group.
The two banks control an estimated 75 percent of the market, it said.
But market dynamics were such that much smaller institutions were able to compete profitably in most business segments, especially residential mortgage lending.
As competition within the market intensifies, the smaller banks need to diversify their revenue sources, it said.
